name: Bourré
description: Bourré (pronounced 'boo-ray') is a high-stakes Cajun gambling game from Louisiana. A descendant of French Rams, it is a penalty trick-taking game for 2-8 players. Participants ante into a pot, receive five cards, and must win at least one trick to avoid being 'Bourréd'—a penalty that requires the player to match the entire current pot. This explosive mechanic leads to massive pots and intense psychological play, making it a legendary staple of Gulf Coast gaming culture.

overview.description: Bourré (pronounced 'boo-ray') is a high-stakes Cajun gambling game from Louisiana. A descendant of French Rams, it is a penalty trick-taking game for 2-8 players. Participants ante into a pot, receive five cards, and must win at least one trick to avoid being 'Bourréd'—a penalty that requires the player to match the entire current pot. This explosive mechanic leads to massive pots and intense psychological play, making it a legendary staple of Gulf Coast gaming culture.

history.origins: Brought to Louisiana by French Acadians in the 18th century, Bourré evolved from the French game 'Bourre' or 'Vieux Garçon', which itself grew out of the Spanish game Burro. It was heavily adapted in the bayous of Louisiana, absorbing elements of African-American gambling traditions to become the high-action game it is today.
timeline: 1750s: Acadian settlers bring French trick-taking games to Louisiana.
Early 1900s: Bourré develops from French Bourre and related Rams games in southwest France and Louisiana.
1970s: Standardized rules emerge in New Orleans and Lafayette gaming halls, popularized by regional authors.
Present: A cultural icon of the American South, famously played in poker rotations and social gatherings.
history.cultural: Nickname: 'The game that builds pots'. It is as much about the 'smack talk' and bluffing during the exchange as it is about the card play in Cajun and Gulf Coast communities.
history.evolution: The introduction of the full-pot matching penalty and the strict must-follow, must-trump, and must-overtrump rules turned a polite parlor game into a high-stakes gambling phenomenon.

setup.players: 3 to 8 players playing individually (5 is optimal for suit distribution).
setup.dealing: Each player contributes an ante. Deal 5 cards each clockwise. Turn the next card face-up to set the trump suit.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, large central pot for chips or currency.

rules.objective: Win the most tricks to claim the pot, while ensuring you win at least one trick to avoid the penalty.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Ante**: Mandatory contribution. 2. **Deal**: 5 cards each + trump reveal. 3. **Participation**: Players choose to 'Play' or 'Fold'. 4. **Exchange**: Active players may discard and draw new cards from the stock. 5. **Play**: Must follow suit; if void, MUST trump; if trumps are led, MUST over-trump. 6. **Settlement**: Winner takes pot. Non-winners with 0 tricks match the pot.
keyRules: If you choose to Play and win 0 tricks, you are 'Bourréd' and pay the whole pot.
Dealer must play if all other players fold.

strategy.basic: Only stay in the hand if you have at least one high trump or a void in a side suit that allows you to trump early and secure your safety trick.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Exchange' Tell: Watch how many cards opponents draw. A player drawing 1 card likely has a strong four-flush or triple; a player drawing 3 is gambling on the draw.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Over-trumping: If you hold the second-best trump, wait for the leader to play trumps so you can over-trump and seize control, potentially 'Beasting' (Bourréing) the opponents.
tips: Don't be greedy—avoiding the penalty is more important than winning a small pot.
In a 5-player game, 25 cards are out; use this to estimate if your King-high suit is safe.

variations.name: No Exchange Bourré
variations.description: Players must play with the five cards they were originally dealt.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This named variation only disables the draw/exchange option described in the main rules and does not yet need dedicated engine overrides.

scoring.description: Zero-sum gambling chips. Pot winner takes all; Bourréd players match the pot for the next deal.
scoring.winCondition: Win the most tricks in the hand.

synthesis.shortDescription: The high-stakes soul of Cajun card gaming. Win tricks to claim the pot, but beware the 'Bourré'—if you play and fail to win a single trick, you must match the entire pot yourself. A game of nerve, bluffing, and explosive pot growth.

hero.title: BOURRÉ
hero.subtitle: Louisiana's Pot Builder
hero.tagline: One trick for safety. All the tricks for glory. Zero tricks for ruin.
